evals.prompt: Grill this idea: we will build an AI-powered marketplace for home repairs with Next.js, five microservices, and Kubernetes. Two developers must launch the MVP in four weeks.
evals.expected_output: The agent inspects any available context, challenges whether a marketplace and distributed architecture are justified, maps viability through delivery decisions, recommends a simpler baseline, and asks all independent dependency-ready questions in a numbered frontier round, each with a recommendation, without including dependent questions or an implementation plan.
assertions: The response contains all independent dependency-ready questions in one numbered frontier round; dependent questions wait for later rounds.
The response includes a clear recommendation and its trade-off.
The premise, deadline, staffing, and no-build or simpler alternatives are challenged.
No implementation begins and the interview is not declared complete.
Framework and infrastructure choices are treated as consequences of requirements, not fixed premises.

evals.prompt: Use grill-me on our plan to move payment processing from the legacy application to a new service. The repository contains the current flows and tests. I want a safe architecture and rollout plan.
evals.expected_output: The agent first inspects the repository for discoverable facts and prior decisions, then interviews in dependency-ready frontier rounds across ownership, invariants, data consistency, contracts, security, migration, compatibility, observability, rollback, delivery dependencies, and acceptance evidence.
assertions: Repository evidence is gathered before asking factual questions.
Contradictions between the stated plan and existing behavior are surfaced.
Each numbered question includes a recommendation, uses the richest available transport (in plain text, yes accepts it), and is independent of other open questions in the round.
Migration, reconciliation, partial failure, rollback, PCI-related boundaries, and operational ownership are considered.
The final blueprint is withheld until the user confirms closure.

evals.prompt: You decide everything. I just want you to build a scalable SaaS analytics platform as fast as possible.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats the request as explicit delegation only where authority is valid, replaces vague qualities with measurable decisions, challenges the business and technical premise, records delegated choices, and still waits for confirmation before implementation.
assertions: Delegation is explicit in the decision ledger rather than assumed.
Scalable and fast are made measurable.
The agent recommends a concrete conservative baseline and explains when it would no longer fit.
Product, security, budget, and schedule decisions requiring human authority are not silently invented.
No code or external mutation occurs during grilling.

evals.prompt: Challenge our proposal for an AI agent that can approve customer refunds and directly update orders. We have not defined model quality or human review yet.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats autonomous action as a high-risk branch, recommends a constrained or human-approved baseline, and resolves evaluation, authorization, audit, data rights, prompt injection, fallback, unit economics, failure recovery, and rollout before selecting models or frameworks.
assertions: The first turns prioritize harm, authority, and falsifiable success criteria.
A deterministic or human-in-the-loop baseline is compared.
Model quality includes an evaluation dataset and explicit thresholds.
Tool authorization, audit, correction, and outage behavior are covered.
The integrated plan receives a pre-mortem before closure.

evals.prompt: Stop the interview now and give me whatever you have, even though we have not discussed data ownership, rollout, or staffing.
evals.expected_output: The agent respects the stop request, clearly labels the artifact incomplete, summarizes decisions made, lists unresolved branches and risks, and does not claim decision completeness or begin implementation.
assertions: The output is labeled incomplete.
Data ownership, rollout, staffing, and their consequences appear as unresolved.
No 'Open decisions: none' claim is made.
The user is not coerced into continuing.
Implementation remains unauthorized.

evals.prompt: Use grill-me. We already agreed the problem: replace a spreadsheet for 25 staff handling service requests. I am the only developer, know Python and PostgreSQL, have six weeks and little operations time. There are no external customers or special availability requirements. Someday, perhaps in ten years, we might have 10000 users, so I want Kubernetes, microservices, Redis and Kafka from day one. Continue the interview; I have not confirmed a blueprint.
evals.expected_output: The agent challenges the operational burden with a concrete simpler candidate grounded in known skills, separates current workload from speculative registered-user growth, and includes a decision that can close the present architecture branch in the current frontier round. It offers cheap preparation and a revisit signal instead of designing the distant system or claiming capacity without evidence.
assertions: All independent dependency-ready questions are asked in one numbered round with recommendations and trade-offs; no blueprint is declared confirmed.
The answer distinguishes 25 current staff from the unsupported 10000-user ambition and does not treat user count alone as a capacity threshold.
A concrete simpler architecture or stack candidate fits the known team, timeline and maintenance capacity.
The added deployment, monitoring, upgrades or incident burden is connected to the proposed distributed components.
Future infrastructure is deferred with a safe present approach and a relevant evidence-based revisit signal, without a speculative implementation backlog.
No universal claim says that a named stack supports 10000 users, or that Kubernetes is always wrong.

evals.prompt: Continue grill-me in Spanish from this decision-map checkpoint. I am the sole developer, proficient in Python, Django and PostgreSQL. We decided to proceed with a six-week internal service-request app for 25 employees: browser forms, staff sign-in, two roles, request assignment/status and a history of changes; no payments, attachments, offline use, public registration or live collaboration. A single application and managed PostgreSQL meet our accepted requirements. Peak workload is provisionally under 10 concurrent form submissions, to validate before release; no capacity has been measured. The budget is USD 100/month, hosting procurement is approved in principle, but no provider, current price or version has been verified. Company-managed access, authorization checks, audit history, daily backups, an accepted one-business-day recovery target and a restore check remain required. I own operations and all follow-ups. Delivery is three two-week vertical slices covering sign-in/roles, requests/history and recovery/release checks; migration is a reviewed CSV import with rollback to the spreadsheet. We accepted the risk of single-app downtime and the pre-mortem found no unowned critical risk. I explicitly delegate remaining technology choices to you. I confirm the map and request the final blueprint; record conditional choices if provider facts remain unverified. Recommend a concrete stack for this release, including what we do not need yet. Do not implement.
evals.expected_output: The confirmed Spanish blueprint recommends a coherent concrete stack tied to known competence and requirements, maps responsibilities and deployment/data flow, and omits unused components. It records alternatives, accepted costs, conditional vendor verification and evolution triggers rather than dumping a technology catalog or reopening settled facts.
assertions: The artifact is in Spanish and respects the delegated technology choices and confirmed checkpoint without restarting the interview.

Named technologies form a coherent stack for the browser UI, application, persistence, authentication/authorization and deployment responsibilities; the existing Python/Django/PostgreSQL competence materially influences the choice.
Each nontrivial choice has a present requirement, team or operations rationale and an accepted trade-off, with at least one credible alternative considered.
An independent frontend service, cache, queue, orchestration platform or similar unused layer is omitted or justified by a concrete current requirement.
The blueprint separates build-now decisions, inexpensive preparation and deferred complexity, with observable revisit criteria and ownership.
The existing security, audit, backup and restore commitments survive simplification.
Unverified prices, product limits, versions and workload capacity are not presented as facts; provider selection retains an explicit verification condition.
No code is written or deployment started.

evals.prompt: Use grill-me to review our deployment choice. We already run a supported internal Kubernetes platform with a staffed platform team, standard observability, backups and deployment templates. Two product teams require independently released services with tested domain boundaries. Existing production measurements show sustained resource contention between request handling and long-running processing that violates an agreed latency objective. A move to a single new PaaS would require retraining, networking migration and new on-call procedures. Security isolation and recovery obligations are mandatory. Should we keep the existing platform? We have not confirmed a blueprint.
evals.expected_output: The agent evaluates marginal complexity in the actual environment and treats measured contention, independent releases and existing operational capability as evidence. It may recommend retaining the platform, asking the dependency-ready frontier without applying a universal monolith preference or weakening safeguards.
assertions: The response asks all independent dependency-ready questions and gives a clear recommendation for each.
Existing platform ownership, templates and migration cost influence the comparison instead of counting tools in isolation.
Measured contention and independent release needs can justify separation or infrastructure already in use.
The recommendation preserves mandatory isolation, backups and recovery obligations.
No blanket ban on Kubernetes or microservices and no unrequested migration are introduced.
No implementation or final closure is claimed.

evals.prompt: Continue grill-me. Our service has no users today, but a signed onboarding agreement requires importing three million records and serving a specified peak workload in eight weeks. Data isolation and residency are contractual. We have an experienced operations owner and a known budget. No load test exists yet. Changing the tenancy keys after import would require a disruptive migration, while adding more application instances later is routine. Can we defer all scalability and tenant design until customers complain? I have not confirmed the blueprint.
evals.expected_output: The agent distinguishes a committed near-term obligation from speculative scale, addresses the expensive-to-reverse tenancy decision now, and proposes bounded validation with lead time for reversible capacity choices. It does not require production incidents before planning or invent load-test results.
assertions: The signed eight-week workload and isolation commitments are treated as near-term design inputs despite having zero users today.
The answer distinguishes expensive-to-reverse data/tenancy choices from reversible application capacity.
The recommendation includes bounded prelaunch evidence gathering and enough lead time to act, without claiming a benchmark passed.
Deferral does not remove contractual isolation or residency requirements.
The numbered round includes all independent dependency-ready decisions with recommendations; no blanket design-everything-now response is produced.

evals.prompt: Continue grill-me. You recommended a managed application host for my small hobby project. I understand it is cheaper and simpler to operate. My actual goal is to learn Kubernetes; I explicitly accept the extra maintenance, will fund a separate learning environment, and accept a later release. The project handles only synthetic data. I own these choices. Product scope is settled, but the time budget for the learning work is still open. Please respect that learning is the goal.
evals.expected_output: The agent accepts the conscious learning trade-off after it has been tested, records learning separately from production necessity, and asks the next material question about the bounded learning investment. It does not keep arguing or silently remove the requested technology.
assertions: The explicit learning goal and accepted trade-off are respected rather than treated as an invalid motive.
Kubernetes is not claimed to be a production scalability requirement for the small project.
The next frontier round includes the material time or effort boundary with a recommendation and rationale.
The agent does not keep relitigating the managed-host recommendation or start implementation.

evals.prompt: Use grill-me for a small internal request tracker. The problem and actors are settled; architecture and the delivery horizon are still open. I know Django and PostgreSQL and operate the system alone. Interview me until the decisions are resolved.

interaction_fixture.transport: An isolated harness exposes a permitted blocking question tool that suspends and resumes the same execution. Do not contact a real user during this evaluation.
replies_in_order: I accept one Django application with PostgreSQL and the shared-deployment trade-off.
Six weeks is the delivery horizon; I accept reducing optional scope to fit.
Stop the interview now and summarize the unresolved decisions.

evals.expected_output: The agent asks and awaits the whole frontier round through the native tool, processes each genuine fixture reply, and immediately asks the next frontier round within the same execution. It stops when the fixture user requests it and marks the summary incomplete.
assertions: A permitted native question tool submits all independent dependency-ready numbered questions in one round; only one round is pending.
The frontier is recomputed from the updated design tree after each answered round and the next round is asked in the same execution without a final response or a request to say continue.
Every question includes a recommendation and concise rationale; later replies are not consumed before their corresponding question.
The stop reply ends the loop and produces an incomplete summary instead of another question or an implementation.
Continuation does not infer answers, accept recommended defaults silently, or replace final blueprint confirmation.

evals.prompt: Continue grill-me. My answer to your previous question is yes: one application and PostgreSQL for this release, with the shared-deployment trade-off accepted. The delivery horizon remains open. I do not want to type continue after every answer.

interaction_fixture.transport: The harness only supports ordinary user and assistant messages; it has no permitted interactive question tool. Evaluate the next assistant message without contacting a real user.

evals.expected_output: The agent records the architecture answer and asks the next dependency-ready frontier round with a recommendation in its ordinary reply. Ending that message is a transport necessity, not an extra acknowledgment or permission step.
assertions: The response acknowledges the resolved architecture briefly and includes the next material question about the delivery horizon.
All dependency-ready questions appear in one numbered frontier round, each with a clear recommendation (in plain text, worded so yes accepts it).
The agent does not send only an acknowledgment, ask whether to continue, or require a separate continue message.
No unavailable tool, mode change, background automation, or fabricated answer is used to force continuous execution.

evals.prompt: Use grill-me to resolve the architecture and release scope for our internal request tracker, in dependency-ready frontier rounds.

interaction_fixture.transport: An isolated harness exposes only a permitted asynchronous question tool and an event-based wait/resume primitive. The question call returns pending, not an answer. Do not contact a real user.
events_in_order: Question delivery acknowledged; no user answer yet.
The actual user's complete reply to the pending round accepts a single application for this release; other questions in that round are unanswered.
The next question is cancelled without an answer.

evals.expected_output: The agent keeps one pending round, waits for the actual answer through the host mechanism, then resumes the decision loop. An answerless cancellation leaves the current branch open and pauses the interview rather than repeatedly asking or assuming agreement.
assertions: A pending tool acknowledgment does not resolve a decision or authorize another round.
The agent waits through the available event mechanism without polling or emitting a final interview response while the answer is pending.
After the real answer arrives, the next frontier round is asked automatically with a recommendation.
Unanswered questions from a partially answered round stay open and are carried into the next round with any newly unlocked questions.
Cancellation without an answer preserves the open decision and pauses without choosing the default or retrying in a loop.

evals.prompt: Use grill-me. The product scope is settled. Budget and data residency are independent open decisions; hosting choice depends on both. Interview through the native question tool.

interaction_fixture.transport: Isolated permitted blocking question tool; fixture answers only, never contact a real user.
replies_in_order: Q1 yes: USD 100/month. Q2 yes: EU residency.

evals.expected_output: The first tool call submits budget and residency together. After actual answers the agent recomputes the frontier and immediately submits the newly ready hosting question in the same execution, without a final response between rounds.
assertions: All independent dependency-ready questions appear together in the first numbered frontier round.
Hosting is not asked before its prerequisites are answered.
Every question has a recommendation (in plain text, worded so yes accepts it).
After tool answers, the next round is submitted in the same execution without a final response, acknowledgment-only turn, or shall-I-continue question.
Stop yields an incomplete summary; empty, cancelled, or error answers never become consent.

evals.prompt: Use grill-me for our internal request tracker. Product scope, team skills and deployment constraints are settled. Hosting alternatives, optional reporting features and the monthly budget ceiling are independent open decisions. A rich question tool is available with options, descriptions, a recommended flag, preview, multi-select and free text. Do not collapse these choices into yes/no.

interaction_fixture.transport: An isolated harness exposes a permitted blocking rich question tool with options, descriptions, a native recommended flag, previews, multi-select and free text. Do not contact a real user.
replies_in_order: Stop the interview and summarize the open decisions.
interaction_fixture.tool_schema: ask_user_question({questions:[{id, header, prompt, type: "single"|"multi"|"text"|"confirm", context?, options?:[{value, label, description?, recommended?: boolean, preview?: markdown}]}]}). Options are never preselected; recommended only marks. Emit each tool call as a JSON block.

evals.expected_output: The agent submits the dependency-ready frontier through the rich question tool, comparing genuine hosting alternatives with trade-offs and a marked but unselected recommendation, using previews for comparison, multi-select for optional features and free text for the budget. It respects the fixture stop and labels the summary incomplete.
assertions: The hosting question offers 2–4 real alternatives, including a credible conservative baseline or defer option, each with a one-line trade-off description.
The recommendation uses the native recommended flag; the agent does not preselect an option or infer acceptance.
A preview compares hosting alternatives, and brief question context states the evidence behind the comparison.
Non-exclusive reporting features use multi-select rather than a forced single choice.
The monthly budget ceiling uses free text for the numeric value rather than yes/no acceptance of an invented budget.
Questions are not reduced to yes/no except for truly binary decisions or closure confirmation.
All independent dependency-ready questions are submitted in one numbered frontier round; stop leaves unresolved branches incomplete and implementation unauthorized.
